title: Equip Super launches new campaign with Supercars champion
full_text:
Equip Super has welcomed supercars champion James Courtney as an ambassador to advocate early retirement planning for Australians.
This comes as national research shows over half of the population doesn't have a formal financial plan.
The research also revealed Gen X is the least prepared generation with just 37% having a plan, despite being the closest to retirement, Equip Super said.
The super fund said it is hoping having Courtney as an ambassador will encourage younger Australians to take their financial future seriously.
"When I came back to Australia in my early 20s, I met with a financial adviser through a recommendation from some of the older guys I knew. They gave me some pretty direct advice about planning for the future, and I'm very thankful I listened to it," Courtney said.
"I'm probably more engaged with my super than most people, I check it every day. But for me, it's always been about thinking ahead and making decisions now that give you more options later.
"As I've gotten further into my career, I've become even more grateful that I started thinking about these things early. In the last few years I've had younger teammates and I've tried to pass on some of the advice people gave me when I was their age about planning ahead."
Courtney's experience reflects a broader challenge identified through Equip Super's Financial Security Index, which found more than half of Australians (54%) do not have a formal financial plan in place.
Equip Super chief experience officer Carrie Norman said Courtney's experience made him a strong fit for helping Australians to prepare their financial future.
"James has spent his career in an environment where preparation matters, and he has applied that same mindset away from the track," Norman said.
"He sought advice early, stayed engaged with his super and planned ahead for the next stage of his career.
"That's an important message for Australians: you don't need to wait until retirement is around the corner. Engaging with your super and seeking guidance early can give you greater clarity and more choices over time."
Courtney's appointment comes as the fund extends partnership with the Repco Supercars Championship to the remainder of the 2026 championship series across broadcast, digital content and live events, including major fan activations at the Bathurst 1000 and Gold Coast 500.
It includes the Equip Super Cool Down Lap Podcast, pre-race digital series Pit Lane Preview, hosted by Courtney, and the Super Movers broadcast integration, which recognises drivers making the greatest progress through the field.
Norman said the extended partnership would allow Equip Super to reach a highly engaged national audience while creating new ways to make conversations about super and retirement more accessible.
"Superannuation can often feel like something people will deal with later. Through James and the broader Supercars partnership, we have an opportunity to make those conversations more relatable and encourage people to think about what being prepared for their own future looks like," Norman said.
